liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Peggy-O** (2 reviews): Following Looks Like Rain, it is described as equally powerful; Considered one of the best versions, but the tape cuts out at the climax of Garcia's solo [8][10]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review, 1 other source): Largely spoiled by badly out-of-tune or misplayed notes from Jerry; Uncle John's Band and U.S. Blues were played as the encore [1][15]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Reviewer ranks this as probably their favorite 1977 version of the song [8]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): First-set closer of about seven minutes, called the finest music of 1977, better than anything from Cornell [17]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Second-set gem going into Morning Dew, though the transition is not as hoped [9]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Terrapin into Dew is the obvious highlight; a preview jam comes before the last verse [16]
- **Around & Around** (1 review): The last three songs are danceable and energetic [9]

## The recordings

- **gd77-06-07.sbd.hollister-bode.24291.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 182 min; rated 4.71/5 by 14 [1]. Said about its sound: A few audio problems appear, but overall the sound is good [16]
- **gd1977-06-07.mtx.seamons.99001.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 183 min; rated 4.57/5 by 7 [2]
- **gd1977-06-07.aud.bertrando.31951.flac16**: audience recording; 22 songs; 182 min; rated 5/5 by 10 [4]. Said about its sound: Mics were bumped and adjusted after Jack Straw; a channel drop-out in Morning Dew into Around & Around is cross-faded to mono [4]
- **gd1977-06-07.144910.akg.d224.bertrando.troy.miller.smith.sirmick.flac1644**: source not stated; 22 songs; 187 min [5]. Said about its sound: Tape pauses smoothed and small patches added; a few sections have tape deterioration, and Funiculi Funicula is slightly clipped [5]

## Around the show

- Reviewer calls it one of the weaker shows of a great period; the next two Winterland nights were better [7]
- First set is called standard for 1977; reviewer has not heard the following two nights [9]
- Overshadowed by other 1977 shows; the June 9 second set is said to be far stronger [12]
- Reviewer finds the March 1977 run superior to the June Winterland run [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd77-06-07.sbd.hollister-bode.24291.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>MR>DAT with AMR>DAT Patches [1]. Also: Reviewer received this version from David Hollister, edited it lightly, and found it wasn't listed on etree, so circulated it [14]
- **gd1977-06-07.mtx.seamons.99001.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC>AIFF>Final Cut>WAV>FLAC) [2]. Also: DAT-to-CD transfers with patches by David Hollister; his original transfer dates to about 1999; Keith Bode edited patches to match volume of the soundboard, converted to SHN and uploaded in May 2004 [2]
- **gd1977-06-07.aud.bertrando.31951.flac16**: source: AUD, Likely: MAR > Reel > DAT > CDs (See note below) [4]. Also: Probably taped by Bob Menke and Reinhardt Hollwein with AKG D224 mics and a Tandberg 10XD deck; Appears to come from the same circulating audience sources as the 6-8-77 and 6-9-77 tapes [4]
- **gd1977-06-07.144910.akg.d224.bertrando.troy.miller.smith.sirmick.flac1644**: taped by Sandy Troy; transferred by Matt Smith, Charlie Miller, Sirmick; source: AKG D224s > Tandberg 10X > 10 in Master Reel @ 7.5 ips - Taped by Sandy Troy and provided by Charlie Miller [5]
